races.title: State House, District 27
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Rodney D. Pierce
cands.bio: Democrat representing North Carolina House District 27 (Halifax, Northampton and Warren counties) since January 2025. Former middle school social studies teacher of nearly a decade and historian. Worked earlier in municipal government, hospitality and media. Won the 2024 primary over incumbent Michael Wray and beat him again in 2026.

endorsements.text: Listed in his 2026 Ballotpedia survey (self-reported): Gov. Josh Stein, former U.S. Reps. Eva Clayton and G.K. Butterfield, NC State AFL-CIO, NC Association of Educators, Sierra Club NC, NC League of Conservation Voters, Planned Parenthood Votes! South Atlantic, Pro-Choice North Carolina, Carolina Forward and Progressive Caucus of the NC Democratic Party.

cands.gaps: We could not find when or why Pierce's family moved from Maryland to North Carolina. We found no bills he sponsored and no documented actions in office on data centers, property taxes, land buying, growth, immigration, guns, abortion, policing or school choice. We found no statements from him on those topics beyond teacher pay. His campaign site and surveys discuss affordable housing, public education funding, rural health care and infrastructure in general terms only. We found no documented controversies, foreign ties, or stated positions on data centers or development.

local.label: Roots 90: Ballotpedia lists his birthplace as Landover, Maryland, while Wikipedia says he grew up in Roanoke Rapids and he describes himself as a lifelong Halifax County resident who graduated from Halifax County Schools.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Has served in the NC House since January 2025. Taught middle school social studies for nearly a decade, worked in municipal government, hospitality and media, and holds an associate degree in paralegal technology and a B.A. in criminal justice.
qual.why: He has legislative experience, though only about one term, plus paralegal and criminal justice training and some local government work. Teaching is not directly legislative work, and advisory committee seats were not counted.
qual.label: He has legislative experience, though only about one term, plus paralegal and criminal justice training and some local government work. Teaching is not directly legislative work, and advisory committee seats were not counted.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Said in his 2024 Ballotpedia survey that he would raise teacher pay to at least the national average and increase per-pupil funding. This covers teacher pay only; the page gives no position on vouchers, charters or school choice.

prio.label: Matches 1 of 1 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 1 only promised (needs 2 to score)

cands.name: David Woodson
cands.bio: David Woodson is a retired Defense Department employee with 38 years of federal service at the Pentagon. He managed printing facilities for the Office of the Secretary of Defense, was Director of Printing at the White House for two years, and retired from the Secretary of the Navy's office. He has not held elective office.
cands.gaps: We found no record of Woodson's stance on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on out-of-state or institutional land buyers, gun laws, or specific school-choice policies. We found no confirmed date for his move to North Carolina and nothing on where he was raised. We found no documented actions in office, since he has never held office. We found no news coverage of him, no endorsements, and no controversies. His career details come only from his own Ballotpedia survey answers. His 2026 survey does not repeat his work history.

land.label: 2 documented positions for data centers or more development

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: He worked 38 years in Defense Department civilian service, managing printing facilities and the Navy's Publications Management Program. He describes experience in budgeting, policy and contracting and in leading teams. He has not held elected office and lost the 2020 and 2026 NC House races.
qual.why: He has management and government-process experience from a long federal career, which fits the middle band. He has no legislative service, no elected office and no documented law, policy or budget career, so he does not reach the high band. The budgeting and policy claims are his own account from a candidate survey.

workers-first.evidence: In his 2020 Ballotpedia survey, Woodson said he would work to prohibit "Sanctuary Cities."

back-police-order.evidence: In his 2020 Ballotpedia survey, Woodson said he supports law enforcement and called the "progressive liberal approach to crime" a failure.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: In his 2020 survey, Woodson said he wants to attract and keep quality educators with retirement healthcare benefits and bonuses, and that a fair wage matters. He gave no specific raise figure and did not mention vouchers or charters.

pro-life.evidence: In his 2020 survey answer about Republican Party principles, Woodson wrote that the party defends "the unborn and the new-born." This is a general statement and names no specific abortion policy.

prio.label: Matches 4 of 4 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 4 only promised

land_positions.quote_or_summary: In his 2026 survey, Woodson said North Carolina is growing and that "District 27 can benefit from that growth with the right leadership." He also said he wants to preserve farms, land and the rural way of life, and to fund water, sewer, roads and broadband for economic development.

In his 2020 survey, Woodson said he would push the Department of Commerce and EDPNC to bring development projects to the district. He also said he would support business incentives to attract investment and seek funds for a "spec building."
